text.p: Xerox Corp. said Thursday that its profits grew by 15 percent in the second quarter, although the strong dollar hurt revenues.
The giant maker of copiers and other office products said its net income for the three months ended June 30 rose to $337 million, or 94 cents a share, from $293 million, or 81 cents a share.
The earnings per share were well ahead of Wall Street expectations of 89 cents a share, according to First Call, which tracks analysts' estimates.
Xerox stock gained 50 cents to $80.50 in early trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was among the 20 most heavily traded issues.
The company said the income included $13 million, or 4 cents a share, realised from its acquisition last month of Rank Group's remaining interest in Rank Xerox.
Xerox, based in Stamford, Conn., said revenues grew by 3 percent to $4.4 billion from $4.2 billion.
However, excluding the impact of currency translations, Xerox said, revenue expanded by 6 percent, driven by strong growth in equipment sales and document outsourcing.
Xerox said sales of its digital products grew 24 percent in the quarter, driven by excellent growth in colour copiers and printers and strong growth in high-speed laser printers.
The DocuColor 40, its 40-page-per-minute colour document processing system, continued to contribute significantly to revenue growth, it said.

Xerox said production publishing revenues showed good growth, despite some slowdown due to new product anticipation. Customers delayed purchases during the period in anticipation of a new 180-page-per minute DocuTech Production Publisher, which is now widely available.
Digital product revenues represented 34 percent of total second-quarter revenues.

"Customer acceptance of the digital black-and-white copiers we introduced in April has been excellent," said Paul Allaire, chairman and chief executive. "Orders for these products have been more than double our expectations."
Allaire also said that the new digital production publishing and printing products that Xerox introduced in May have received excellent customer acceptance.

Sales of black-and-white light-lens copiers declined 3 percent in the quarter, reflecting pricing pressures and the impact of customers transitioning to Xerox digital technology. They now account for 52 percent of total revenues,

The company said that as a result of its focus on productivity and expense controls, the ratio of selling, administrative and general expenses to revenues improved by a half percentage point to 29.6 percent.
